title: Insulin Signaling Pathway Analysis in Mice
author: Fawaz G. Haj
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.yp2fvqe
materials: Use cervical dislocation to euthanize mice.

steps.title: Fast Mice
steps.instruction: Fast the mice for 16 hours by removing food at 3:00pm the day before the procedure.

steps.title: Administer Insulin
steps.instruction: Give the mouse an intraperitoneal injection of insulin (10 U/kg) using a 27 G needle.

steps.title: Collect Blood and Plasma
steps.instruction: Collect the maximum amount of blood from the portal vein and isolate plasma according to standard protocols or P.I. specifications.

steps.title: Collect and Process Tissues
steps.instruction: Quickly collect Liver, Muscle, Adipose, and Pancreas tissues, completing the entire collection process within a maximum of 3 minutes.

substeps.instruction: Divide each tissue into three portions.
Snap freeze the first portion in liquid nitrogen.
Place the second portion into RNA later solution.
Fix the third portion in the appropriate fixative solution.

steps.title: Prepare Tissues for Western Blotting
steps.instruction: Lyse the tissues into the appropriate lysis buffer for western blotting.

steps.title: Analyze Insulin Signaling Phosphorylation
steps.instruction: Determine the phosphorylation states of insulin signaling components using immunoprecipitation and western blotting.

substeps.instruction: Determine overall and site-specific tyrosyl phosphorylation of IR and insulin receptor substrates (IRSs) via immunoprecipitation (IP) and probing with phospho-tyrosyl antibodies according to standard protocols.
Determine tyrosine, serine, and/or threonine phosphorylation of other components, such as Akt and MAP kinases, according to standard Western blotting protocols.
